title: Quarter Starter: ORION playbook and exec brief
content:
Purpose and context:
This is the ORION quarter-starter playbook: a compact, pragmatic run of decisions, OKR candidates, and an all-staff run-of-show to get the company aligned for the next 90 days. Intended audience: execs, product leads, eng managers, and people owning cross-functional rollouts.

Summary headline (for Exec Update):
- Overall ask: focus resource weight on three production levers that materially improve unit economics and reliability: (1) Reduce 95th-percentile latency across hosted API by 20% via batching and kernel tuning; (2) Ship Dedicated capacity SLA & autoscaling revamp to unblock two large enterprise renewals; (3) Launch Private deploy self-onboarding beta with KMS integration and 3 pilot customers.
- Why now: model ecosystem fragmentation + increased customer MLP demands mean we must prove both reliability and economics simultaneously.

Proposed company-level OKRs (ORION draft)
Objective O1 — Make inference predictable at scale (customer-facing SLOs)
KR1.1: Reduce Hosted API p95 generation latency from baseline by 20% for top 5 most-used models (measured over 7d windows).
KR1.2: Increase default autoscale smoothness (no cold-start spikes) so incidents attributable to scale churn drop to <=2 per quarter.
KR1.3: Customer-observed error rate for production traffic <=0.5% across Hosted & Dedicated.

Objective O2 — Improve unit economics while preserving output quality
KR2.1: Ship intelligent batching and cache configuration defaults that cut per-token cost by 15% for general-purpose workloads in the hosted tier.
KR2.2: Release a quantization recommendation guide and two validated quantized model variants with measured quality delta <=2% on benchmark prompts.
KR2.3: Reduce tail GPU utilization inefficiency (idle time due to small requests) by 25% via prefix-KV caching and packing.

Objective O3 — Win enterprise operational trust and enable private deployments
KR3.1: Deliver Private onboarding beta (3 customers) with KMS + audit logs + e2e test suite in 60 days.
KR3.2: Completed Dedicated SLA revamp published and approved by legal + two enterprise customers committed to renew under new terms.
KR3.3: On-prem runtime packaging: produce a reproducible install that passes our internal compliance checklist (list included below).

Notes on measurables and instrumentation:
- Metrics owners: infra-metrics for latency and utilization (Tom Hsu), serving-runtime for batch kernels (Jun Park), product-managed telemetry for customer-facing SLOs (Maya Rivera).
- Define measurement windows and baseline dates by end of week 1. Use consistent cohort (top 5 models by tokens) for cross-quarter comparison.

All-staff kickoff & run-of-show (draft)
- Duration: 90 minutes (company-wide). Hybrid: in-person + livestream. Recorded.
- Goals: align on 3 company priorities, surface ridges/risks, lay out owner-level commitments and clear next steps.
- Agenda (timestamps):
  - 0–10 min: Opening & CEO framing (why ORION matters)
  - 10–25 min: Product update — hosted improvements + model catalog highlights (product lead)
  - 25–40 min: Engineering highlight — Dedicated SLA revamp & autoscale work (eng lead)
  - 40–55 min: Private deploy beta plan & compliance (security & solutions eng)
  - 55–70 min: Customer success spotlight — enterprise renewals & asks (CS lead)
  - 70–85 min: Rapid Q&A + live poll on tradeoffs (poll: latency vs cost vs features)
  - 85–90 min: Clear next steps, owners, and how to follow up (ops)
- Pre-reads: 1) short one-pager (this doc condensed to 2 pages), 2) telemetry baseline deck (two slides), 3) risk register (below). Pre-reads circulated 72h before the event.

Communications plan (post-kickoff)
- Exec summary (3 bullets) to be emailed to company within 24h + pinned channels summary in #all-staff.
- Teams must publish one-line commitment in team channels within 48h (owner + first deliverable date).
- Weekly ORION sync (30m) for owners — sync cadence starts immediately, shared notes in the ORION confluence page.

Decision log (to capture during planning week)
- D1: Prioritization lens for tickets: must map to at least one KR or get explicit exec exception.
- D2: Two-week freeze on major API surface changes during initial rollout window to reduce combinatorial regressions.
- D3: Default batching settings will be opt-out for hosted tier for first 30 days after rollout.

Risk register (top items and mitigations)
- Risk R1: Quality regressions from quantization or kernel changes. Mitigation: gated rollouts, model-level A/B with production shadowing, and prompt-set regressions tracked by Product Evals.
- Risk R2: Enterprise pipelines delayed due to compliance questions. Mitigation: ship trimmed Private beta that isolates KMS + logging features, produce compliance doc with SOC-like artifacts. Assign: Elena Gomez + Legal.
- Risk R3: Unexpected cost spike from autoscale misconfiguration. Mitigation: safety budget cap and rate limiter with rollback policy; simulate worst-case load in staging. Assign: SRE (Brandon Lee).

Operational checklist for Private beta (minimum required)
- KMS integration tested end-to-end (encrypt keys, rotation doc)
- Audit-trail sample export and queryable UI
- Network connectivity pattern docs (VPC peering and firewall templates)
- Containerized on-prem bundle and reproducible install script + acceptance tests
- Support-runbook for first 30 days (on-call rotation + escalation map)

Owner-level commitments (first pass)
- Product (Maya Rivera): OKR definition finalization, pre-read telemetry deck, customer shepherding for pilots. Target: 2026-03-01.
- Serving Runtime (Jun Park): batching kernel rollout + quantized model validation. Target: 2026-03-31.
- Infra/SRE (Tom Hsu): autoscale tuning + safety guardrails. Target: 2026-03-24.
- Security & Compliance (Elena Gomez): Private beta compliance pack. Target: 2026-03-15.
- CS & Solutions (Brandon Lee): identify 3 pilot customers, run onboarding rehearsals. Target: 2026-03-08.

Open questions (to resolve in week 0)
- Q1: Which three models should be the ORION cohort? Proposed: default LLM-anchor, medium-sized conversational, and a high-throughput embeddings model. Need product agreement.
- Q2: What is the exact threshold for "cost improvement" KR measurement across heterogeneous workloads? Proposal: standardize on a synthetic reference workload + two customer workload proxies.
- Q3: Who signs the updated Dedicated SLA (legal vs CRO vs CFO) and what is an acceptable indemnity band?

Next steps (immediate 10 days)
- Day 0–2: Finalize OKRs and measurement definitions (Exec + Product + Eng).
- Day 3–6: Produce pre-reads and short telemetry baseline slides; finalize run-of-show.
- Day 7–10: Circulate invites, rehearse with presenters, lock recording/stream infra.

Appendix: quick template for team one-line commitment (post-kickoff)
- [Team name] owner: [Owner name] — commit: [short deliverable], by [date], depends on [team(s)]. Example: Serving-runtime owner: Jun Park — commit: "Batching kernel v1 rollout to hosted-stage" by 2026-03-17, depends on infra/SRE.

Tone and expectations:
- This is deliberately compact. The playbook is an action-first artifact: produce clear owners and measureable KRs, minimize open-ended artifacts. We will iterate the ORION OKRs after the first two weekly syncs.

If you want me to convert this into a 2-slide pre-read and a 1-page email blurb for distribution, say so and I will produce drafts (slide bullets + email copy).

-- end of draft ORION playbook (v0-1)
